title: Potato, mashed, from dry mix, NFS

content.title: About
content.content: The dry mix for mashed potatoes (NFS) provides a convenient way to obtain smooth mash without boiling and mashing fresh potatoes. The mix typically contains dehydrated potato, salt, spices, and sometimes dry dairy ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dry mash mixes are widely used in cafeterias and catering to speed up preparation.
Modern drying technology preserves much of the flavor and texture of fresh potatoes.
The formulation may include additives such as dry cream or milk powder to enhance creaminess.
The mix is shelf‑stable, requiring no refrigeration and having a long shelf life.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The mix provides complex carbs that deliver sustained energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It retains vitamin B6 and B3, important for metabolism.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, supporting heart and muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike mash made with butter, the dry mix is low in fat unless added during cooking.

items.title: Convenience
items.content: Quick preparation saves time, which is beneficial for busy schedules.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some mixes contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Dairy or gluten may be present; check the label if you have allergies.

items.title: Nutrient loss
items.content: Prolonged storage can degrade certain vitamins, so freshness matters.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Combine the mix with hot water or milk in the ratios indicated on the package, stir vigorously until smooth, and serve hot. Optional additions include butter, cheese, or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry mix in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use within a few months for best quality.
